target_moa.text: Osimertinib is a kinase inhibitor of EGFR that binds irreversibly to certain mutant forms of EGFR (T790M, L858R, and exon 19 deletion) at ~9-fold lower concentrations than wild-type; it also inhibits HER2, HER3, HER4, ACK1, and BLK

osimertinib also inhibits the activity of HER2, HER3, HER4, ACK1, and BLK.

Osimertinib is kinase inhibitor of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), which binds irreversibly to certain mutant forms of EGFR (T790M, L858R, and exon 19 deletion) at approximately 9-fold lower concentrations than wild-type.

key_safety.text: Most common (>20%) adverse reactions: diarrhea (42%), rash (41%), dry skin (31%), nail toxicity (25%). Most serious adverse reactions were interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, cardiomyopathy, and QTc prolongation; fatal ILD occurred in ~0.5% of patients

citations.quote: In Studies 1 and 2, the most common (>20%) adverse reactions (all grades) observed in TAGRISSO-treated patients were diarrhea (42%), rash (41%), dry skin (31%), and nail toxicity (25%).

The most serious adverse reactions of osimertinib identified across all clinical studies (n=813) were interstitial lung disease, cardiomyopathy, and QTc prolongation. Fatal ILD and fatal cardiomyopathy occurred in approximately 0.5% and 0.2% of patients, respectively.

detail.text: REMS not required; risks of ILD/pneumonitis and QTc prolongation can be mitigated through product labeling

citations.quote: Both the clinical review team and the DRISK reviewer agreed that risk evaluation and mitigation strategies (REMS) are not required to ensure safe and effective use of osimertinib and that the serious risks of interstitial lung disease/interstitial pneumonitis and QTc prolongation can be mitigated through agreed-upon product labeling.

basis.text: Granted priority review (reviewer recommendation: Priority Review) because osimertinib treats a serious, life-threatening condition (metastatic NSCLC) and provides a significant improvement in effectiveness over available therapy

citations.quote: ## **Recommendation:** Priority Review

Metastatic NSCLC is a serious and life-threatening disease with a predicted 5-year survival of 4.2%. Even in the subset of NSCLC with an EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC, the median survival ranges from 19-28 months.
